1. The Airport Spur contributes 3dBA to the 1990 predicted noise levels and results in noise levels higher than the standards adjacent to the Spur between South 13th and South 20th Streets.
2. Predicted 1990 inside and outside noise levels at Hamlin Garland School during normal school hours will both be approximately 3dBA higher than the noise standards.
3. If the Airport Spur was not constructed, the 1990 predicted noise levels along I-94 would still be 12dBA higher than the standards.
4. Existing noise levels adjacent to I-94 are 8dBA higher than the noise standards.
Since some of the existing noise levels for the study area are above the standards and the 1990 noise levels without abatement would be above the standards, noise abatement will be provided to reduce the noise levels to meet the standards.
Twenty-six noise measurement sites were investigated. Their locations are shown in Figure 19. Forty-five minute noise measurements were taken at each site for three measurement periods corresponding to the morning rush hour (6:30-9:00  AM), midday (11:00  AM-2:00  PM), and evening rush hours (4:00-6:30  PM). The noise measurements were taken during these periods in an effort to obtain the greatest existing noise levels. The L<sub>10</sub> noise level measurements (dBA) are shown in Figure 20.
